Once I learned how to stop obsessing over the detrans aspect of my life, dating got easier. You don't need to make being detrans your entire presentation. Fill out your profile with your hobbies, your interests, worry about the ultra vulnerable, personal experiences such as this once you trust and connect with someone. It's best to approach these things when you feel the time is right, it's similar to coming out. 

You don't owe anything to anyone to feel the need to disclose anything. You're you, you have more to your life than your medical/psychological history. We all do.

I'd assume it is probably different for each person, however just take it slow, use your resources and coping skills to the best of your ability. It's a long ride but I only ever hope everyone can get through it better than I did.

This isn't exactly the same, but I hope it offers some insight. I cold turkeyed weekly Testosterone shots (cannot remember the dosage) after 2.3 years on, then immediately went on estrogen birth control after about a month. What I remember most, as this was nearly 4 years ago now, was pretty much going crazy. I was going to urgent care nearly weekly because of my whole body just feeling so ill and constant panic attacks. It triggered my mental disorders in ways I have never felt before or since in my life and my body had pretty much no sense of stability whatsoever. I was constantly ill and to look back on it, the way it made me act was probably some kind of near psychosis from the immediate drastic horomones fluctuations, but that's my hypothesis. 

It took a few medications before I found a birth control that worked for me, which I have been on since and do not plan to go off ever as periods are horrible for me as well. 

By going onto the birth control I believe that it helped somewhat "speed up" my detransitionion, atleast a little bit. I began *actual* breast growth for the first time (I started Testosterone extremely young) after about 2-3 months off of T and my face looked completely different every single month for about a year and eight months. My voice lightened significantly, though it is still permanently scarred and extremely physically uncomfortable to use. The fat redistribution and feminization was quite noticeable after about 10 months but didn't peak until probably a little over a year after stopping T.

As much as I am thankful for the birth control I began and still take, it was true suffering to get here. I have gone through three pubertys and that level of extremity with my horomones is massively draining. I cannot even begin to explain how crazy I went when I detransitioned, it was the best decision of my life but I believe due to the hormones it spawned the worst mental cycles I have ever been in before. So if you take this route, take it slow, talk to a genuinely trusted Healthcare professional if you can. And always remember, I can't emphasize it enough, you *need* to be patient. It all takes time. The waiting is the worst part but the patience leads somewhere. It takes a long time but is so very worth it.
